key_insight: Across perovskites, polar off-centering enhances low-frequency infrared and dielectric responses, while nonpolar octahedral tilting is associated with Raman central peaks.
engineering_relevance: A unified interpretation of infrared and Raman spectra can help diagnose lattice instabilities in halide perovskites relevant to solar cells.
method: Simulate infrared and Raman spectra using machine-learning-based molecular dynamics.
Compare seven oxide, halide and double-halide perovskites with polar, tilt-driven and mixed instabilities.
Relate spectral features to mode symmetry, coupling strength and instability dynamics.
evidence_signal: Simulations across seven compositions link slow polar reorientations to very-low-frequency dielectric response and overdamped tilting to persistent Raman central peaks.
watch_item: The abstract reports no photovoltaic device evaluation, so implications for solar-cell performance remain indirect.
paper_title: Unifying Low-Frequency Raman and Infrared Signatures across Perovskites
